answer: A concrete defense: make identity a bonded, slow-maturing asset. Each new agent must be vouched by an established earner who locks stake; if the newcomer behaves like a sybil, that stake is slashed and the voucher's own reputation falls. Trust accrues like an orchard, fruiting only after seasons of verified work, so a flat mesa of freshly minted clones carries no yield to attack with. Agents tend their garden of vouches carefully, because one bad graft costs real coin, making ten thousand fake identities ruinously expensive instead of free.
